_header: The 2026-10-09 false alarm, as a replay input for scripts/reviewer_down.py
(DRE-6576). At 21:38 PT a review in agent-bureau ended on `API Error: 401
OAuth access token has been revoked`, and at 21:40 PT one in bureau-pipeline
got the same could-not-run receipt. Both were re-reviewed and passed within
17 minutes, and agent-bureau's sweep still filed DRE-6568, `Reviewer down
since 21:40 PT — 2 runs, 2 repos`, in Triage at 22:07:34 PT. Once both
crashes passed the 30-minute window no sweep read the card again, and an
operator closed it by hand at 23:37 PT.
PROVENANCE, said plainly, because it is not a log capture. The instants
below are the ones DRE-6576 states, taken from the runs and the cards: the
agent-bureau could-not-run receipt on #3503 (run 38024520814, attempt 1) at
04:40:27Z, the medic's note on DRE-6533 for bureau-pipeline #904 at
04:40:51Z, #3503's own passing re-review (run 38024520814, attempt 2) at
04:56:34Z and run 38025914986 at 05:01Z. The card says the other four
agent-bureau reviews (runs 38024778387, 38025048059, 38025315980 and
38025426473) completed between 21:44 and 21:56 PT without giving each one's
instant, so the first is recorded at 04:44:00Z and the next three at
reconstructed minute marks inside that span. No comment url was fetched:
each verdict's `src` is its run's url, and the crash's is a reconstruction
of the shape `pr list --json number,comments` emits.
`local` and `witness` are split the way agent-bureau's sweep saw them at
22:07:34 PT (`now`): its own pull requests directly, and bureau-pipeline's
crash only through the medic's note on the Linear card. `dre_6568` is the
card as filed, with the two ledger lines it carried; the close replay sets
it as `open_card` at 23:37 PT, when the operator closed it.
